column1: # The coverage ratchet baseline — doc:35-testing#coverage.
# module, missed instructions, missed branches, covered instructions, covered branches.
# All four figures are EXACT bounds: the build fails when a module's count differs from
# its row in either direction, so both halves of the ratio move only through this file.
# Regenerate with ./gradlew coverageBaselineWrite, and review the diff. The writer
# REFUSES to raise a missed count; a deliberate regression needs
# -Pcoverage.regress=<reason>, and the reason is recorded below.

# REGRESSION accepted with -Pcoverage.regress: identity validators replaced two three-branch isNotBlank() && none{} checks with single whole-string regex matches; six branches disappear from the source, none become uncovered (missed branches stay 0)
#   :core-domain: covered branches 44 -> 38

# REGRESSION accepted with -Pcoverage.regress: GrantIssued stores its capabilities as a Set rather than a List, so three toSet() calls disappear from equals, hashCode and the field initialiser; six instructions leave the source, none become uncovered (missed instructions stay 0)
#   :core-domain: covered instructions 1549 -> 1543
# Restored by hand after coverageBaselineWrite erased it, one entry per bean and summed from
# the list rather than counted beside it: bean:0032 (1), bean:0030 (1), bean:0036 (2),
# bean:0065 (1), bean:0066 (2), bean:0147 (3) = 10. Written out per bean because a bare
# total beside the enumeration it summarises is made wrong by the next commit that extends
# the enumeration, which happened here twice (bean:0033, bean:0173).
# The writer also erases a PREVIOUS regression
# block when recording a new one, which is what it did to bean:0065's block on the run below.
# bean:0065 is the cleanest instance yet: the writer destroyed all six lines on a run in
# which NO figure changed, because it rebuilds the file from a constant header plus rows and
# the note it composes is empty unless THIS run regressed. bean:0066 saw it destroy the block
# on a run that moved two rows UPWARD, so the defect is not conditional on the direction of
# the write either.
# bean:0147 saw it a ninth time, on the rebase onto this very file: a run that moved
# exactly ONE row upward (:adapter-persistence-flatfile 0 -> 778) destroyed all three
# REGRESSION blocks above and this note with them. That is bean:0066's shape confirmed
# independently, and bean:0147 also saw the worse form — a run that legitimately
# RECORDED a regression erased the two blocks that preceded it, so recording a
# regression costs every regression recorded before it. Both are written up in
# bean:0033, observations seven and eight.
# bean:0033 makes it survive.

# REGRESSION accepted with -Pcoverage.regress: InProcessDomainEventDispatch moved from core-application to the new adapter-events-inprocess module on the PR 83 review ruling; 39 covered instructions and 4 covered branches leave core-application with their class and reappear in the adapter's row, none become uncovered (missed instructions stay 6)
